content: According to new figures, private consultants were paid £3.4bn by public bodies in the last year, a 62% increase from 2019-20. The data also highlighted that spending on consultants, which surged during Covid, remains higher than pre-pandemic levels. The statistics underscore the task facing Keir Starmer’s government, which seeks to cut consultant expenses by half. The Financial Times recently reported that KPMG secured a government contract worth up to £223m for civil servant training. Since the Labour party came to power, almost £650m in new government contracts have been awarded to consultants. The deal with KPMG is the second-biggest public sector contract awarded to the consultancy firm. Labour peer Prem Sikka criticised the practice, describing it as part of a culture of unnecessary consultant hiring. Is there anything else I can help with?
